checks: The same-wave strict increment excludes unequal positive class volumes. When N=1, M=a exhausts the measured trace.

For N≥2 each strict level below a has the same N-point class support. The accepted parity-rank integrand gives (s+1)N−s(s+1)/2. Its excess over 2N−1 is (s−1)[N−(s+2)/2], strictly positive for s≥2. Therefore s=1.

The line through integer endpoints has lattice p_0+Z v for primitive v. Same parity makes the far endpoint an even number of primitive steps away because v has an odd coordinate. Interpolation of the endpoint fibers puts volume ≥a at every intervening integer site. Counting the even sites gives L=N−1, and equality forces all 2N−1 fibers to have volume a and every other fiber to have zero d-volume.

Containment of the midpoint body and equality of the three volumes forces equality in ordinary Brunn–Minkowski. Equal positive volumes make the endpoint homothety a translation. Convexity then includes each affine translate and equal positive volume upgrades inclusion to equality. The mass count also proves the converse.

The base-fixing shear aligns the translated bodies without changing their volumes. The selected middle centroid belongs to its actual fiber. For nonconstant continuous traces, opposite shifts on each pair give 2Γ_d a and the middle gives Γ_d a. For a pure base cap the closed boundary keeps the middle and at least one member per pair, so the mass is at least (L+1)a≥Γ_d M. Zero-mass fibers cause no change.

Original bbc972e469554176 §§2–3 give the same chain and actual point. The final quantitative depth is stronger than the source's NΓ_d a bound by using both tails rather than one paid fiber from each pair.
